**Finding: Missing (critical) — no Client-side ownership provision.**

What I found:
- **§2(d) (p0029)** is the only ownership clause and runs one way: "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface." That is acceptable in itself (Vendor keeping its platform), but there is no counterpart confirming what we own.
- **Deliverables gap:** §4 Support Services has TrueLink's programmer building work for us, yet no clause allocates ownership of those results — leaving TrueLink's IP definition (p0017, which sweeps in "improvements, works of authorship, materials... tools") to arguably capture them.
- **Data gap:** Client Content (p0011) and Client's Intellectual Property (p0012) are defined but never tied to Client title; §10 only makes them Client Proprietary Information for confidentiality purposes, which is not an ownership right.
- **§8(d) (p0054):** we grant TrueLink a broad licence to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit" Credit Data with no statement that we retain title. I left this negotiated bargain intact (already narrowed by the Credit Data definition and the Non-Competition Agreement) and instead clarified it is a licence only, not a transfer of ownership.

Redline (validated, inserted as new §2(e) after p0029): we retain all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, the Web Site and all borrower/loan and other Client data; TrueLink assigns the results of the Support Services and other deliverables to us; TrueLink keeps its pre-existing IP and grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to any TrueLink IP embedded in deliverables; no joint ownership. The comment offers the licence-only fallback if TrueLink resists assignment.
